title: Zetwerk Lists at 5% Premium in $2.7 Billion Debut as Early Backers Book Up to 38x
excerpt: The B2B manufacturing platform opened near Rs 499 against a Rs 475 issue price on the NSE, marking Peak XV Partners' 30th listing, before slipping below issue price intraday.
body:
• Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses listed on the NSE at about a 5% premium — opening near Rs 499 against an issue price of Rs 475 — valuing the B2B manufacturing platform at about $2.7 billion.
  • The Rs 3,650 crore IPO was subscribed about 1.5 times; the stock slipped below its issue price during its debut session before recovering.
  • Early backers booked paper gains of up to 36-38x: the listing was Peak XV Partners' 30th, with Lightspeed, Kae Capital and Accel also among the early investors.
  • Zetwerk reported revenue of about Rs 11,769 crore and an order book near Rs 41,000 crore, with roughly 27% of revenue from overseas markets.

Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses made a measured stock-market debut on Friday, listing on the National Stock Exchange at about a 5% premium to its Rs 475 issue price and valuing the Bengaluru-based B2B manufacturing platform at roughly $2.7 billion, before the shares slipped below the issue price during the session in a reminder of how cautiously Indian investors are pricing new listings.

The stock opened at Rs 498.85 on the NSE, up 5.02%, and at Rs 496.95 on the BSE, according to Moneycontrol. VCCircle reported the shares later traded below the Rs 475 issue price during the debut session. The Rs 3,650 crore (about $412 million) public issue — a fresh issue of about Rs 1,650 crore alongside an offer for sale of about Rs 2,000 crore — was subscribed roughly 1.5 times, with qualified institutional buyers taking about twice their quota and retail investors about 1.35 times.

A payday for early venture backers

The listing's headline numbers belong to Zetwerk's earliest investors. It is Peak XV Partners' 30th portfolio listing, and early backers including Lightspeed India, Kae Capital and Accel are sitting on paper returns reported at up to 36-38 times their initial cheques. Kae Capital, among the first believers in the company founded in 2018 by Amrit Acharya, Srinath Ramakkrushnan, Rahul Sharma and Vishal Chaudhary, is the standout: its first fund's stake was reported worth about $70 million at listing prices. Peak XV managing director Shailesh Lakhani called Zetwerk the firm's eighth portfolio company to cross $100 million in revenue, and Acharya the "de facto leader" of precision manufacturing in India.

"Zetwerk is our eighth portfolio company to cross $100M in revenue — Amrit is the de facto leader of precision manufacturing in India."

— Shailesh Lakhani, Managing Director, Peak XV Partners

The business behind the ticker

Zetwerk runs a managed marketplace that matches manufacturing orders — precision components, capital goods, consumer electronics, building materials — with a network of small and mid-sized factories across India and Southeast Asia. It reported revenue of about Rs 11,769 crore for FY25 on VCCircle's figures, an order book of roughly Rs 41,000 crore, and international revenue of about 27% of the total, a mix that has made it a reference point for the "China-plus-one" shift in global sourcing. Moneycontrol has reported the IPO leaves the company with a large cash reserve after the OFS-heavy structure.

What to watch

For diaspora investors who follow Indian listings through GIFT City and NRI demat routes, Zetwerk is a test of appetite for B2B industrial platforms as opposed to consumer names: a 1.5x subscription and a mid-single-digit listing premium are respectable, not euphoric. Whether the stock holds above its issue price in the coming weeks will depend on quarterly order-book conversion, not on the debut-day tape.
